messages.content: Hello! Today we are going to learn one of the most confusing concepts for beginners in JavaScript: Closures.
I often struggle to distinguish the difference between a closure and regular function scope.
No problem. Take a look at the definition and code examples on the right first, and then we'll break down the execution process together.

components.title: Closures
components.definition: A closure is a function that has access to its free variables. In other words, a closure gives you access to an outer function's scope from an inner function.
components.example:
function makeFunc() {
  var name = 'Mozilla';
  function displayName() {
    alert(name);
  }
  return displayName;
}

var myFunc = makeFunc();
myFunc();
